feastLines.line: 📓 Journal: the man in his 40s, with ink-stained fingers, the surgeon taught the man in his 50s, with a crooked nose Wound Care.
👀 "surgeon, huh?" the man in his 40s, with ink-stained fingers, the surgeon nods — then, an hour later, drops a shop-talk detail no surgeon would ever get right. They catch themselves. Too late.
👀 You caught the man in his 40s, with ink-stained fingers, the surgeon rehearsing — muttering details about Denver under their breath before the evening fire, like someone cramming for a part.

🔥 The fire settles. the man in his 30s has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "A heron that isn't quite there when you look at it — I put it down today." "The heron is gone. No — it's there. It was always there. You just couldn't see it until it moved." "You blink. It is somewhere else. You didn't see it move." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Maya says quietly "Say that again — slower." the man in his 40s, with ink-stained fingers, the surgeon mutters "So it bleeds." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we call

🔥 The fire settles. Sergio has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "A toad like a war drum, throat swelling — I put it down today." "Its throat swells. The air goes thick. Every frog for a mile answers at once." "It crouches — clumsy, obvious, and faster than it looks." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. the woman in her 30s, with thick glasses asks "The fire feels smaller now." Penelope breathes "The fire feels smaller now." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Sergio has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "A gold flash in the grass, gone when you look — I put it down today." "Its scales go from dull brown to molten gold. Heat shimmers off its back. It's ready." "It goes still in the sun. Gold spreads across its back — the charge is building." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. the woman in her 40s mutters "So it bleeds." the man in his 40s, with ink-stained fingers, the surgeon says quietly "Did it look at you? Before?" Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — wh
the man in his 40s, with ink-stained fingers, the surgeon came back from the treeline white-faced. Saw it too. Whatever it is, it's still out there.
👀 Someone asks Jerónimo a shop-talk question about surgeon work. The pause before the answer is long enough to hear.

🔥 The fire settles. Tashi has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Drum-Belly — I put it down today." "It rears up, belly swelling drum-taut, and beats it with both paws — BOOM. The air itself flinches." "It waddles left, then is suddenly right — a feint, testing whether your eyes or your ears are in charge." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Penelope mutters "And you're still standing." Luis breathes "So it bleeds." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Jerónimo has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Flashbulb Moth — I put it down today." "It lands. It folds its wings. The light in the clearing changes, like someone adjusting a lamp." "It lets go of the air and simply... drifts. Somewhere else. Hard to predict." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Tashi asks "Did it look at you? Before?" Maya mutters "Did it look at you? Before?" Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Sergio has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "The Mountain Lord — I put it down today." "It crouches low, tail lashing once, twice. The stripes go still. Then it comes." "A paw rises, claws out — casual, almost lazy. It is not lazy." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Luis breathes "We've been walking past those." June mutters "The fire feels smaller now." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Miriam has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Hushpuppy — I put it down today." "No telegraph you can hear. Watch the birds — when they go quiet, the pack is already moving." "The pack circles — nips from the edge, never committing." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Jerónimo asks "Tell me you didn't go alone." Leo says "The fire feels smaller now." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Sergio has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Nevermore — I put it down today." "Its shadow detaches from the branch-shadow and slides across the ground toward you — a straight black lane, growing. The bird hasn't moved. The shadow has." "It climbs, laughing in a dead voice — out of spear reach, watching." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Jerónimo says "The fire feels smaller now." Olivia asks "Tell me you didn't go alone." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Maya has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "Inspiration — I put it down today." "It brightens. The light is too white, too certain. EUREKA — the biggest burst so far." "It flickers — a smaller, meaner idea. Less certain, faster." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Leo breathes "We've been walking past those." Jerónimo says "The fire feels smaller now." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"

🔥 The fire settles. Penelope has been quiet all evening, and now everyone knows why. "The Understudy — I put it down today." "It watches your weapon. It lifts its own — a perfect, insulting copy at half fidelity." "It starts performing — and your most-used move is suddenly anticipated, halved, ANSWERED." A beat of silence, then the questions come all at once. Nikos says "So it bleeds." Luis mutters "Tell me you didn't go alone." Someone at the edge of the light says what everyone's thinking: "So — what are we calling it?"
